methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes source structure (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/P.json) for the Pediatrics chapter (160 canonical source nodes). Unlike OR/OT, P's toc_inventory.json extraction is clean, single-column, and well-organized (17 system-based L2 sections each with atomic disease/topic-level L3 children); the vast majority of nodes required no structural correction. Targeted verification (raw OCR of the chapter's own TOC page and of body pages for headings whose title suggested a multi-disease umbrella, per the workflow's instruction to split broad nodes only when body evidence confirms distinct topics) surfaced four categories of correction, each independently confirmed via raw OCR body-page text and documented in the affected units' structural_rationale: (1) an entirely uncatalogued section -- 'Primary Care' (Visit Overview, Routine Immunization, Growth and Development, Nutrition, Injury Prevention Counselling, Circumcision), body-confirmed on pdf 1200-1206/P4-P10, absent from toc_inventory.json and independently flagged as one of P's two UNRESOLVED headings in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json ('PrimaryCaré') -- recovered as six new study units (SU-P-002 through SU-P-007) under synthetic UNCATALOGUED ids; (2) two genuine multi-disease umbrella nodes in Cardiology -- P.S05.T02 'Acyanotic Congenital Heart Disease' (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation, aortic stenosis, pulmonary stenosis) and P.S05.T03 'Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease' (TOF, TGA, TAPVR, truncus arteriosus, HLHS, Ebstein's anomaly) -- each body-confirmed (pdf 1217-1220/P21-P24) to contain multiple independently-testable named lesions with their own definition/epidemiology/investigations/management subsections, split into 11 recovered study units (aortic stenosis and pulmonary stenosis combined into one unit, SU-P-030) while the parent nodes are retained only as organizational-header references; (3) a Neurology umbrella node -- P.S15.T04 'Neurocutaneous Syndromes' -- body-confirmed (pdf 1285/P89) to contain two distinct named syndromes (Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and Type 2, each with its own diagnostic-criteria subsection), split into 2 recovered units; and (4) a Neurology umbrella node -- P.S15.T06 'Seizure Disorders' -- body-confirmed (pdf 1286/P90) to contain a general seizure-management-and-mimics approach plus four distinct named childhood epilepsy syndromes (Infantile Spasms/West syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut, Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy, Childhood Absence Epilepsy), split into 5 recovered units (1 approach + 4 syndrome-specific). Additionally, P.S13.T04 'Common Conditions of Neonates' is body-confirmed (pdf ~1266) to be a nested organizational sub-heading with no independent content of its own (it introduces the already-separately-catalogued T05-T17 specific-condition subsections) and is excluded as organizational rather than represented as its own study unit. All corrections are resolved via raw OCR body-page confirmation (never model memory/medical-knowledge reconstruction) and cited in each affected unit's structural_rationale; no page-image rendering was required as raw-text OCR was internally consistent and sufficient at every point checked. The chapter's other UNRESOLVED heading, 'Acromyms' (source_pdf_page 1197), is confirmed via the same raw-OCR read to be the chapter-opening acronym glossary immediately preceding P.S01 (Pediatric Quick Reference Values) -- excluded as non-clinical, consistent with the chapter-opening acronym-glossary exclusion precedent used in OP.S01/OB.S01/NS.S01/OR.S01/OT.S01. Excluded as non-clinical organizational/reference material: the chapter root (P); the 17 system-level L2 section headers (S02, S04-S17), which carry no independent content beyond their T-level children; P.S13.T04 (nested organizational sub-header, see above); P.S05.T02/T03 and P.S15.T04 (fully redistributed into recovered per-lesion/per-syndrome units, see above); and P.S18 (Common Medications, a drug-reference table, consistent with the OR.S15/OP.S20/OB.S18/NS.S20 reference-section precedent) and P.S19 (Landmark Pediatric Trials, an EBM/reference appendix). Genuine cross-discipline overlap (Hematology, Respirology-vs-GI Cystic Fibrosis, Respirology-vs-ID Pneumonia, GI-vs-ID Gastroenteritis, Oncology-vs-GI abdominal mass, Development-vs-Neurology hypotonia/motor delay) is recorded via cross_discipline_note on the affected crosswalk entries without finalizing primary ownership, per the pending global cross-discipline audit.

study_units.title: Pediatric Quick Reference Values (Normal Vital Signs by Age)
study_units.structural_rationale: P.S01 is a chapter-opening reference block (Table 1 normal HR/RR by age, Table 2 normal SBP by age, Table 3 normal temperature ranges/measurement) immediately following the excluded chapter-opening acronym glossary (raw OCR of pdf 1197/P1-1199/P3 confirms the acronym table is directly followed by these normal-value tables, matching the chapter-opening acronym-then-reference-values pattern). Retained as a single foundational reference unit distinct from the acronym glossary itself.

study_units.title: Well-Child Visit Overview (Approach to the Pediatric History and Periodic Health Encounter)
study_units.structural_rationale: The 'Primary Care' section heading is entirely absent from toc_inventory.json and is independently flagged as one of P's two UNRESOLVED headings in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json ('PrimaryCaré', source_pdf_page 1197). Raw OCR of the chapter's own TOC page (pdf 1197) confirms the real structure: 'PrimaryCaré... Visit Overview Routine Immunization Growth and Development Nutrition Circumcision' appears between 'Pediatric Quick Reference Values' (P.S01, P3) and 'Common Complaints' (P.S02, P10) -- i.e. a real, substantial, clinically important section (well-child care) with five subtopics that toc_inventory.json omits entirely. Body-confirmed via raw OCR of pdf 1200-1206 (P4-P10): Visit Overview (history-taking approach, HEEADSSS/SSHADESS, ITHELPS) on P4-P5; Routine Immunization (adverse reactions/contraindications table) on P5-P6; Growth and Development (growth chart use, Fenton curve, developmental milestones table) on P7-P8; Nutrition (breastfeeding/formula, signs of adequate/inadequate intake, foods to avoid) on P8-P9; a sixth body heading not named in the TOC line itself, 'Injury Prevention Counselling' (age-banded injury-prevention counselling table), on P10 immediately before Circumcision; and Circumcision (elective-procedure counselling) closing the section on P10, directly followed by 'Common Complaints' / 'Breath Holding Spells' (P.S02.T01) on the same pdf page (1206). All six subtopics are represented under synthetic UNCATALOGUED ids (UNCATALOGUED:PrimaryCare@pdf1200.T0N) per the established recovered-heading convention (cf. OT's Hearing section, SU-OT-04/05). No page-image rendering was required; raw-text OCR was internally consistent at every point checked.

study_units.title: Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD)
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's P.S05.T02 ('Acyanotic Congenital Heart Disease') is a single umbrella node, but raw OCR of pdf 1217-1219 (P21-P23) body-confirms it groups multiple genuinely distinct named lesions, each with its own definition/epidemiology/clinical-features/investigations/management subsection: Ventricular Septal Defect ('most common congenital heart defect, 30-50%'), Atrial Septal Defect (3 subtypes), Patent Ductus Arteriosus, Coarctation of the Aorta, Aortic Stenosis, and Pulmonary Stenosis. Per the instruction to split broad TOC nodes only when body evidence confirms distinct topics (and not to fragment generic sub-headings within one disease), each of these six named lesions -- which are independently testable diagnoses with their own diagnostic criteria -- is recovered as its own study unit under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id, while P.S05.T02 itself is retained only as the parent umbrella reference in source_hierarchy_path.

study_units.title: Atrial Septal Defect (ASD)
study_units.structural_rationale: See VSD unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Acyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; ASD is body-confirmed on pdf 1217 (P21) with its own definition (3 subtypes: ostium primum, ostium secundum, sinus venosus), epidemiology, natural history, and management.

study_units.title: Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)
study_units.structural_rationale: See VSD unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Acyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; PDA is body-confirmed on pdf 1218 (P22) with its own definition, epidemiology (especially prematurity), clinical features, and management including indomethacin.

study_units.title: Coarctation of the Aorta
study_units.structural_rationale: See VSD unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Acyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; Coarctation is body-confirmed on pdf 1218-1219 (P22-P23) with its own definition, Turner-syndrome/bicuspid-aortic-valve associations, and management (prostaglandins to maintain ductal patency in severe neonatal presentation).

study_units.title: Aortic Stenosis and Pulmonary Stenosis (Valvular Obstructive Lesions)
study_units.structural_rationale: See VSD unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Acyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; Aortic Stenosis and Pulmonary Stenosis are body-confirmed as adjacent, parallel-structured subsections on pdf 1219 (P23), each with valvular/subvalvular/supravalvular subtypes and analogous investigation/management (balloon valvuloplasty for valvular disease, surgery for sub-/supravalvular disease); grouped into one unit given their near-identical teaching structure and shared 'obstructive lesion' classification (physical exam: decreased urine output, pallor, cool extremities, poor pulses, shock, or sudden collapse if severe).

study_units.title: Tetralogy of Fallot
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's P.S05.T03 ('Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease') is a single umbrella node, but raw OCR of pdf 1219-1220 (P23-P24) body-confirms it groups multiple genuinely distinct named lesions, each with its own figure and definition/pathophysiology/management subsection: Tetralogy of Fallot, Transposition of the Great Arteries, Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return, Truncus Arteriosus, Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, and Ebstein's Anomaly (the last as a labeled sidebar box with its own Etiology/Treatment). Each is recovered as its own study unit under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id, matching the Acyanotic-CHD split rationale above; P.S05.T03 is retained only as the parent umbrella reference in source_hierarchy_path.

study_units.title: Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA)
study_units.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; TGA is body-confirmed on pdf 1219-1220 (P23-P24) with its own definition, physiology (parallel systemic/pulmonary circulations, survival dependent on mixing via PDA/ASD/VSD), and management (prostaglandin E1, balloon atrial septostomy, arterial switch).

study_units.title: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR)
study_units.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; TAPVR is body-confirmed on pdf 1220 (P24) with its own definition, pathophysiology, and management (urgent surgical repair for severe cyanosis).

study_units.title: Truncus Arteriosus
study_units.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; Truncus Arteriosus is body-confirmed on pdf 1220 (P24) with its own definition/pathophysiology (single great vessel overlying a large VSD) and management.

study_units.title: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS)
study_units.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; HLHS is body-confirmed on pdf 1220 (P24) with its own definition (LV hypoplasia, atretic/stenotic mitral and/or aortic valve, small ascending aorta, coarctation), ductal-dependent systemic-circulation physiology, and management (prostaglandin E1, surgical palliation, or transplant).

study_units.title: Ebstein's Anomaly
study_units.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; Ebstein's Anomaly is body-confirmed as a labeled sidebar box on pdf 1219 (P23) with its own Etiology/Treatment content (malformed, apically-displaced tricuspid valve leaflets; association with maternal lithium/benzodiazepine use in the first trimester; association with accessory conduction pathways such as WPW).

study_units.title: Approach to Pediatric Seizures (General Management, Seizure Mimics)
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's P.S15.T06 ('Seizure Disorders') is a single umbrella node, but raw OCR of pdf 1286 (P90) body-confirms it groups a general seizure-management/investigation approach together with four distinct, individually-named 'Childhood Epilepsy Syndromes' subsections (Infantile Spasms, Lennox-Gastaut, Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy, Childhood Absence Epilepsy), each with its own definition/EEG-finding/management block, before cross-referencing the adult Neurology chapter (N19) for Generalized and Partial Seizures. The general-approach content (investigations, seizure mimics box, medication-initiation principles, ketogenic diet, legal driving-reporting obligation) is retained as this standalone unit; the four named epilepsy syndromes are recovered as their own study units below under synthetic UNCATALOGUED ids.

study_units.title: Infantile Spasms (West Syndrome)
study_units.structural_rationale: See 'Approach to Pediatric Seizures' unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Seizure Disorders umbrella-node split. Infantile Spasms is body-confirmed on pdf 1286 (P90) as explicitly labeled a 'pediatric emergency' given risk of developmental regression, with its own onset age, clinical description, EEG finding (hypsarrhythmia), and management.

study_units.title: Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome
study_units.structural_rationale: See 'Approach to Pediatric Seizures' unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Seizure Disorders umbrella-node split. Lennox-Gastaut is body-confirmed on pdf 1286 (P90) with its own triad definition, onset age, and (often poor) prognosis.

study_units.title: Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (Janz Syndrome)
study_units.structural_rationale: See 'Approach to Pediatric Seizures' unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Seizure Disorders umbrella-node split. JME is body-confirmed on pdf 1286 (P90) with its own definition, adolescent onset, EEG finding, and excellent-prognosis-with-lifelong-treatment note.

study_units.title: Childhood Absence Epilepsy
study_units.structural_rationale: See 'Approach to Pediatric Seizures' unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Seizure Disorders umbrella-node split. Childhood Absence Epilepsy is body-confirmed as the fourth named syndrome on pdf 1286 (P90), immediately following JME (text truncated at 'Childhood Absence E...' in the raw-OCR extraction window but clearly identifiable by heading and standard TN sequence).
